correction.text: Awadh, the province Saadat Khan governed from 1722

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins the Nawabs in 1727. 'He was appointed governor of Awadh (in present-day Uttar Pradesh) on 9 September 1722'; the Nawab page gives formation 26 January 1722 (text: 1724). The page names Awadh only; the province is drawn by the gazetteer's Awadh region.

1727-1743, 102,852 km2 (bbox 79.8-84.4 E, 24.3-28.3 N). The Nawab page gives no area. The shape includes the Benares-Jaunpur-Mirzapur country, which the Benares page says Balwant Singh took over in 1737 'from the Mughal Emperor' as zamindar under the Awadh province; before 1737 this is unverified: page budget. The page lists Bhopal (1737) and Karnal (1739) among the Nawabs' battles, with no territorial change.
1744-1747, 102,668 km2: same shape (one cell). Safdar Jung is Nawab from 1739; no page opened records a boundary change.
1748-1751, 102,587 km2: same shape; no change on the pages opened.
1752-1761, 102,614 km2: same shape. The Nawab page has Awadh join Ahmad Shah Durrani at the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) with no territorial result.

correction.text: shape unchanged for 1762-1764; from 1765 see nawab-of-awadh_1765

keyframe_review.note: 1762-1768, 102,535 km2. Applies as drawn to 1762-1764; from the Treaty of Allahabad of 16 August 1765, when 'Kora and Allahabad district would go to Company', the Allahabad district comes out (new keyframe nawab-of-awadh_1765). Cliopatria's shape holds the eastern half of the Allahabad district (7 cells within 30 km of the city).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1765-1768. 'On 16 August 1765 AD he signed the Treaty of Allahabad, which said that Kora and Allahabad district would go to Company'; 'Awadh gave up first the fort of Chunar, then districts of Benaras, Ghazipur and finally Allahabad' (undated sequence; Cliopatria keeps Benares in Awadh to 1774). Shah Alam II resided in the fort of Allahabad 'for six years' (page: left May 1771).

keyframe_review.note: 1769-1771, 102,614 km2: as 1765-1768, without the Allahabad district while the Emperor holds the fort of Allahabad (until May 1771).

correction.text: Awadh without the Allahabad district and the Doab lands of Kora, until the emperor hands them over (year not on the page; Cliopatria 1775)

keyframe_review.note: 1772-1774, 102,215 km2; applies to 1772-1773 (Rohilkhand falls to Awadh in 1774, see nawab-of-awadh_1774). Shah Alam II 'left Allahabad in May 1771 and in January 1772 reached Delhi'; the page says he 'later also handed over the districts of Allahabad and Kora to the Nawab of Awadh' without a year, so Awadh regains them after 1771; Cliopatria draws the Doab gain in 1775, so the district stays out until then.

The 1796 shape is the one to use for 1794-1795.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1801-1856 (about 47,000 km2 by the gazetteer's cells; Cliopatria has none). The Ceded and Conquered Provinces page: 'The territory included the Gorakhpur and Rohilkhand divisions' and 'the districts of Allahabad, Fatehpur, Cawnpore, Etawah, Mainpuri, Etah', ceded 'in return for protection against a threat of attack from the north-west by Zaman Shah Durrani'. The rump stays a Nawab and, from 1818, a kingdom to its annexation in February 1856; draw it as a British client (lighter tint) from 1801.

region.text: Awadh, governed by Saadat Khan from 1722

ledger.note: 1722: Saadat Khan founds the Nawabi of Awadh. The Nawab page's infobox gives 'Formation 26 January 1722' while the text says 'In 1724, Nawab Sa'adat Khan established the Kingdom of Awadh with their capital in Faizabad and Lucknow'; the Saadat Khan page has him 'appointed governor of Awadh ... on 9 September 1722' and 'first Nawab of the Kingdom of Awadh from 26 January 1722 to 1739' (table: Subadar Nawab 1732-1739).

region.text: Benares and the country round it: Varanasi, Bhadohi, Chandauli, Jaunpur, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra (Benares page) with Ghazipur, the area Cliopatria's Awadh row loses in 1775

ledger.note: 1737: Balwant Singh of Benares takes Varanasi, Chunar and the Jaunpur jagirs as Awadh's zamindar. 'Balwant Singh, the ruler of Utaria in 1737, took over the Jagirs of Jaunpur' and took Varanasi and Chunar 'in 1737 from the Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah'; the first rulers 'were originally Zamindars for the Awadh province of the Mughal Empire'; he 'declared himself Maharaja of Benares in 1740'. From 1737 the state 'included most of present-day Bhadohi, Chandauli, Jaunpur, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra, and Varanasi districts'. Cliopatria draws the country inside Awadh to 1774.

16 August 1765: the Treaty of Allahabad takes the Allahabad district from Awadh. 'On 16 August 1765 AD he signed the Treaty of Allahabad, which said that Kora and Allahabad district would go to Company'; 'the Company would get 5 million rupees from Awadh'. Shah Alam II page: 'The company further secured the districts of Kora and Allahabad.' The pages do not say that Awadh held the districts before 1765; the shape removes the part Cliopatria draws inside Awadh.

1774: Awadh and the Company's brigade invade Rohilkhand. The Rohilla War page dates the war '1773-1774'; 'The Rohillas under Hafiz Rahmat Ali Khan were defeated by Colonel Alexander Champion on 23 April 1774 at the Battle of Miranpur Katra'. First ground taken: April 1774.

7 October 1774: the treaty of Lal Dang ends the Rohilla War. 'on 7 October 1774 Faizullah signed an amicable treaty of Lal Dang'; he received a princely state of his choosing, which became Rampur State.

region.text: Rohilkhand as the Awadh shape holds it from the 1794 row on, without Rampur (Cliopatria's Awadh 1796 shape minus its 1788 shape)

ledger.note: 1774: Rohilkhand falls to Awadh. 'Rohilkhand fell to Awadh, and was plundered and occupied.' Faizullah Khan keeps Rampur (the page calls it a Rohilla state under British protection). The page does not say that Rohilkhand was formally annexed (the infobox lists 'Annexation'). Cliopatria draws the gain in 1794.

region.text: Benares and the country round it: Varanasi, Bhadohi, Chandauli, Jaunpur, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra (Benares page) with Ghazipur, the area Cliopatria's Awadh row loses in 1775

ledger.note: 1775: the Benares country leaves Awadh. 'Between 1775 and 1795, the British gradually took over administration of most of the state.' The Benares page also says the Company 'annexed' the city 'under the Treaty of Faizabad in the later 1760s' and the Shuja-ud-Daula page puts the surrender of Chunar, Benares and Ghazipur among the payments for British protection without a year; Cliopatria draws the loss in 1775, the page's first year of British takeover.

region.text: Benares and the country round it: Varanasi, Bhadohi, Chandauli, Jaunpur, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra (Benares page) with Ghazipur, the area Cliopatria's Awadh row loses in 1775

ledger.note: 1775: Benares and its country pass to the East India Company. Same page and reading as the vassal_end of the same year; Chait Singh rules 19 August 1770 to 14 September 1781 (Benares page table).

region.text: the Doab districts of Kora, Allahabad and Fatehpur-Kanpur-Etawah side that the emperor 'handed over' to the Nawab; the area Cliopatria's Awadh row gains in 1775

ledger.note: 1775 (bridged): Kora and the Doab districts return to Awadh. Shah Alam II 'later also handed over the districts of Allahabad and Kora to the Nawab of Awadh'; the page gives no year (he left Allahabad in May 1771 and reached Delhi in January 1772), and Cliopatria's Awadh row gains the land in 1775 from its Maratha shape. Confidence 1: the year is Cliopatria's.

1775: Asaf-ud-Daula moves the capital from Faizabad to Lucknow. 'In 1775 he moved the capital of Awadh from Faizabad to Lucknow' (marked citation needed); he became Nawab on 26 January 1775 on the death of Shuja-ud-Daula (the page's text says 28 January).

ledger.note: 1801: the Nawab cedes half of Awadh to the Company. 'In 1801, the Nawab of Awadh, Saadat Ali, ceded some territory to the British' 'in return for protection against a threat of attack from the north-west by Zaman Shah Durrani': 'the Gorakhpur and Rohilkhand divisions' and 'the districts of Allahabad, Fatehpur, Cawnpore, Etawah, Mainpuri, Etah'. The page gives no month and no area.

1818: Awadh declares itself independent of the Mughals. 'Oudh State eventually declared itself independent from the rule of the Mughal in 1818.' The Wajid Ali Shah page calls the state a kingdom and Wajid Ali Shah 'the last king of Awadh'. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

ledger.note: 11 February 1856: the Company annexes Awadh. 'was annexed by the EIC on 11 February 1856' (the page's infobox and succession table say 7 February 1856); the British Resident Sleeman had reported 'maladministration' and 'lawlessness'; Wajid Ali Shah was exiled to Metiabruz near Calcutta on 13 May 1856.

ledger.note: February 1856: the Kingdom of Awadh ends. The Nawab page's infobox gives 'Abolition 3 March 1858', the end of the rebel government of Begum Hazrat Mahal and Birjis Qadr (the page lists them as the 12th and 13th Nawabs, 'in rebellion', 11 February 1856 / 5 July 1857 to 3 March 1858).

wars.name: Third Battle of Panipat
wars.outcome: The Nawab of Awadh joined Ahmad Shah Durrani; Shuja-ud-Daula 'commanded a sizeable army of Mughal Sepoy, who cut off the supplies of the Marathas'. No territorial change for Awadh on the pages opened.
wars.note: The Nawab page lists it among the Nawabs' battles; the Shuja page gives no year.

wars.name: Battle of Buxar and the Treaty of Allahabad
wars.outcome: 22-23 October 1764: the Company defeats Shah Alam II, Mir Qasim and Shuja-ud-Daula; 'Shuja-ud-Daula fled west ... eventually surrendered'. 16 August 1765: the Treaty of Allahabad gives Kora and Allahabad district to the Company, with 5 million rupees from Awadh.
wars.note: Treaty terms from the Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II pages, which also say the Emperor then lived in the fort of Allahabad.

wars.name: Rohilla War
wars.outcome: Miranpur Katra, 23 April 1774: Hafiz Rahmat Khan killed; Rohilkhand falls to Awadh; the treaty of Lal Dang (7 October 1774) leaves Faizullah Khan the princely state of Rampur.
wars.note: Awadh paid, or promised, forty lakhs of rupees for the Company's help (the page's 'rods of gold' figure is probably a typo).

wars.name: Cession of 1801
wars.outcome: Not a war: a treaty cession of the Gorakhpur and Rohilkhand divisions and six Doab districts for protection against a threatened invasion by Zaman Shah Durrani.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; the territorial result is in the ledger.

certainty.note: Mughal province and district limits; the Himalayan Tarai frontier, the Doab frontier and the Benares country were never surveyed. The Rohilkhand frontier is fixed by the 1774 treaty of Lal Dang only as far as Rampur.
The frontier with the Company follows the districts named in the 1801 cession; the Nepal Tarai frontier stays soft.

notes: Budget: 9 pages, all used (the tenth try, 'Annexation_of_Oudh', returned url_not_found and was replaced by the Wajid Ali Shah page); the Buxar page was opened for the nawabs-of-bengal dossier and is cited once here. Cliopatria rows: 'Nawab of Awadh' 1727-1802 (13 shapes). The state is drawn from 1722 (new core keyframe) and to the annexation of February 1856; Cliopatria ends in 1802 and gives all of Awadh to its British Empire shape from 1803 (116,334 km2), although the pages show half of Awadh left to the Nawab in 1801 (new keyframe 1801-1856, about 47,000 km2 by cells; the historical figure for the rump is larger and not on a page opened). The rump should be drawn as a British client from 1801; that vassal_start belongs in the british-empire dossier. Corrections: Rohilkhand and Rampur (Cliopatria 1794/1796, pages 1774); the Allahabad district out of Awadh from 1765; the Doab regained after 1771 (year not on the page, Cliopatria 1775, confidence 1). Unverified: the 1788 loss of 4,300 km2 in the north to Cliopatria's Nepal shape (no page opened mentions it; probably a drawing artefact of the Tarai); the 1727-1737 inclusion of the Benares country. Disagreements: formation 26 January 1722 (infobox) / 1724 (text) / appointment 9 September 1722 / Subadar Nawab 1732 (Saadat Khan table); annexation 11 February 1856 (text) / 7 February (infobox); Asaf-ud-Daula's accession 26 or 28 January 1775 and death 20 April or 21 September 1797; Benares annexed 'in the later 1760s' (Benares page) versus 1775 (Cliopatria, 'Between 1775 and 1795'); Kora and Allahabad to the Company (Shuja, Shah Alam pages) versus to the Emperor (not on these pages). The Nawab page gives no area and no capital years; the Awadh keyframes could not be compared with an infobox area. Counterparts needing dossiers: benares-state (the Raja of Benares, vassal 1737-1775), rampur-state (Faizullah Khan, from 1774; rohilkhand-state names it a successor), the Awadh rebel government of 1857-58 (Hazrat Mahal, Birjis Qadr; type rebel). Gazetteer: no places for Kora, Mainpuri, Etah, Farrukhabad, Ghazipur, Jaunpur, Azamgarh, Basti, Chunar, Sultanpur; 'Gorakhpur division' and 'Benares country' are circles and a Cliopatria difference.
